test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sells a printer to B at a loss of 60% and B sells the printer to C at a profit of 25%. If C purchased the printer for ₹89,569 then what was the cost (in ₹) of the printer for A?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price** for **A** be x.

Successive multiplier: x × (100 − 60)% × (100 + 25)% = 89,569.

x × 0.40 × 1.25 = 89,569.

x × 0.5 = 89,569 ⇒ x = 89,569 ÷ 0.5 = 179,138.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹179,138.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Loss of A = **60%**, Profit of B = **25%**, Final Price (C) = **₹89,569**.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 ± Gain/Loss)% ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/822fa8d0f85caa58a6c4e2e2b53870e6385a5efab4a4c5819ae81a4a82452a00.png] 
⇒ Let Cost Price for A = **CPA**.
⇒ SP for A (which is CP for B) = CPA × (40 ÷ 100) = 0.4CPA.
⇒ SP for B (which is CP for C) = 0.4CPA × (125 ÷ 100).
⇒ 89,569 = 0.4CPA × 1.25.
⇒ 89,569 = 0.5CPA.
⇒ CPA = 89,569 × 2 = 179,138.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹179,138.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule in Profit and Loss

When an article is passed through multiple hands, the final price is the product of initial price and successive change multipliers: Final = Initial × (100±r₁)% × (100±r₂)%.

Effective Percentage Change

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%. Here, −60 + 25 + (−60 × 25 ÷ 100) = −35 − 15 = −50% net loss.
